user.title: Connect to Arcane
user.description: Enter the address of your Arcane instance and an API key created under Settings > API keys.

data_description.url: Full address of the Arcane web interface, for example {example_url}
data_description.api_key: An Arcane API key. It needs read access plus permission for the actions you want to control from Home Assistant. Once set up, **Configure > API key permissions** lists exactly which permissions your options need.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off if Arcane uses a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Arcane
reauth_confirm.description: The API key for {url} is no longer accepted. Enter a new one.

data_description.api_key: Leave empty to keep the key that is already stored.

error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to Arcane. Check the URL and that the instance is reachable.
error.insufficient_permissions: The API key is missing the environments:list permission.
error.invalid_url: That is not a valid address. It has to start with http or https.
error.unsupported_version: This Arcane instance runs a version older than 3.0. Update Arcane to 3.0 or newer.

abort.already_configured: This Arcane instance is already configured.

data_description.scan_interval: How often Arcane is polled, in seconds.
data_description.environments: Leave empty to follow every environment Arcane exposes.
data_description.monitor_containers: Create a device with entities for each container.
data_description.monitor_projects: Create a device with entities for each Compose project.
data_description.monitor_resources: Poll the image, volume and network counts and the Docker version.
data_description.host_stats: Take one sample per update over a short lived WebSocket. Off by default because it is an extra connection per update.
data_description.disk_usage: Ask in the background, at most every 15 minutes, how much space unused images, stopped containers, unused volumes and the build cache hold. Off by default because Docker sizes every volume for it, which can take a while on large volumes.
data_description.instant_updates: Keep one request per environment open that Arcane answers as soon as something changes, then update right away instead of waiting for the next interval. Polling continues as before.
data_description.include_internal: Also expose containers Arcane marks as internal.
data_description.include_hidden: Also expose containers hidden in the Arcane interface.

data.entity_prefix: Prefix device names with their kind
data.events: Fire events on the Home Assistant bus
data.arcane_events: Arcane event log on the bus

data_description.update_entities: Offer an update entity per container that installs the newer image through Arcane's updater and shows release notes where Arcane finds them, plus a button per environment that checks for updates right away. An update Arcane holds back cannot be installed.
data_description.health_sensors: Add a Healthy sensor to containers that define a health check.
data_description.entity_prefix: Name devices Container x and Project x so a container and a project of the same name do not collide. Entity IDs that already exist keep their current name.
data_description.nest_containers: Show a container as a child device of the Compose project it belongs to.
data_description.events: Fire arcane_container_state_changed, arcane_container_health_changed and arcane_project_state_changed so automations can react to crashes and health changes.
data_description.arcane_events: Read Arcane's own event log on every update and fire arcane_event for each new entry, such as a container that ran out of memory, an image pull or a login.
data_description.updater: Add a button per environment that installs every pending update the way Arcane's scheduled updates do, a sensor showing that updates are being installed and one with the last update Arcane applied.
data_description.jobs: Add a sensor per background job of Arcane, such as its automatic updates or the image update watcher, with the outcome of the last run, when it runs next and the last error. With control allowed, also a button per job that runs it now.

data_description.allow_control: Turn this off for a read only setup: no switches, buttons or update installs are created.
data_description.redeploy_buttons: Add a button per container and per project that pulls the image again and recreates it.
data_description.auto_update_switches: Add a switch per container that includes it in Arcane's automatic updates or leaves it out. The automatic updates themselves only run when they are switched on in Arcane's settings.
data_description.prune_button: Add a button per environment that removes unused images, networks and build cache. Containers and volumes are never pruned.

missing_permissions.title: Arcane API key is missing permissions
missing_permissions.description:
The API key of {name} was refused for: {permissions}

Until the role behind the key carries these, the parts that need them stay empty or fail when you use them. Add them under **Settings > Roles** in Arcane, or turn those parts off under the integration's **Configure > API key permissions**. The repair clears once the polling gets through again, or when the integration is reloaded.
